solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suggestive rogue ends trail chasing skirt

indicators.note: the trail follows behind the skirt, so it comes after it
the two ends of the word rogue are taken, its first and last letters

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
a scent is the trail an animal leaves

explanation.surface: A rogue follows the trail of a woman, chasing skirt in the old phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing skirt' reads as womanising, but 'chasing' only orders the pieces and 'skirt' is the short one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent calls another thing to mind, so it is suggestive of it.

clue.text: Probe with tool over excavation

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals the word for tool is turned upside down

parts.note: an axe is a cutting tool
a mine is a dug excavation

explanation.surface: An archaeologist probes a dig with a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' signals the tool word read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe something is to investigate it closely, a synonym for examine.

clue.text: Hot worker supporting bar around plough

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes last
the bar word goes around the plough word, enclosing it

parts.note: an inn is a pub or bar
to dig is to work the soil, as a plough does
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A sweaty labourer props up a bar near a plough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts ANT beneath IN(DIG)N in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot under the collar describes anger, and indignant means angered by unfairness.

clue.text: Types dropping line giving opinions

indicators.note: dropping means the line letter falls out of the word for types

parts.note: ideals are perfect types or models

explanation.surface: Kinds of thing losing a line yield points of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes L out of IDEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas can be views or beliefs a person holds, i.e. opinions.

clue.text: Greek character, almost simple, meeting a monster

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for simple is dropped

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: A Greek figure of modest nature meets a monster, as in myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MERE to MER. 'Greek character' looks like a person but is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chimera was a fire-breathing monster of Greek myth, lion, goat and serpent combined.

clue.text: Witnessing that husband gets caught in zip

indicators.note: the husband letter is trapped inside the word for witnessing

parts.note: noting means observing or witnessing
H is the abbreviation for husband in records

explanation.surface: Someone sees a husband snag himself in his trouser zip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets caught in' places H inside NOTING. 'zip' looks like a fastener but means zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is informal for zero, none at all.

clue.text: Secretary two-times, embracing blokes, showing spirit

parts.note: a temp is a temporary secretary

indicators.note: the two time words wrap around the word for blokes

parts.note: two words for time: era, a long period, and T, the abbreviation for time
men are blokes

explanation.surface: A secretary cheats on two partners, cuddling blokes and showing some spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-times' looks like cheating on someone but stands for two words for time; 'embracing' wraps them round the blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperament means character or disposition, here spirit or mettle.

clue.text: Adam's original sin was consistent

indicators.note: original points to the first letter of Adam's name

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Adam's original sin in Eden followed a consistent pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original sin' reads as the theological phrase, but 'original' just takes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that agreed matched, so each was consistent with the other.

clue.text: State of organ after tip's cut

indicators.note: the organ word comes after the trimmed tip
cut means the word for tip loses its last letter

parts.note: an end is a tip
a gland is a body organ

explanation.surface: An organ is in a sorry state once its tip is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the tip word; 'after' puts the organ second.
explanation.definitionFit: England is a country, a state, of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Lives and dies clutching head of sword

indicators.note: the word for dies holds the sword letter inside it

parts.note: exits is a theatrical euphemism for dies

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of sword

explanation.surface: A swordsman lives and dies by the sword, gripping its hilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutching' puts S inside EXITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, so it means lives.

clue.text: Pugnacious one, chap boxing about after gong

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay follows the gong word

parts.note: a bell, like a gong, is struck to ring
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the chap word boxes in the word for about

parts.note: a gent is a chap
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A boxer comes out fighting after the bell rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' and 'gong' build a fight scene but only signal enclosure and a ringing instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerent describes someone eager to fight, aggressive.

clue.text: Combining tart with sugar coating removing top

parts.note: a tart is an open pie

indicators.note: removing top drops the first letter of the sugar coating word

parts.note: icing is a sugar coating on a cake

explanation.surface: A baker finishes a tart with icing, scraping off the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing top' takes I from ICING.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecing things together joins them, combining parts into a whole.

clue.text: Plaster I levelled inside is dry

indicators.note: inside means the letters sit within the run of words plaster I levelled

explanation.surface: A plasterer says the plaster they smoothed is now dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile land is barren and arid, unproductive, so dry.

clue.text: Raised section of arch not opening

indicators.note: not opening drops the first letter of the arch word

parts.note: a bridge is an arch over a gap

explanation.surface: Part of an arch is raised but not open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening' drops B from BRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a raised strip or crest along a surface.

clue.text: Advanced right — then turn left, or port

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
to turn is to change

explanation.surface: Sailing directions: advance to starboard, then turn to port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the left side of a ship, which fits the directions, but it means a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a Russian port on the White Sea.

clue.text: Scoundrel hugging more bashful sweetheart is dismissed

indicators.note: the scoundrel word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel
shier means more shy or bashful
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A cad embraces his shyer sweetheart and is sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the middle letter of sweet; 'is' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer cashiered is discharged from service in disgrace, so dismissed.

clue.text: Following tip, wins match leaving men on board

indicators.note: the match word follows the tip word

parts.note: a tip is a messy place, a mess
a chess player who mates wins the game

explanation.surface: After a tip-off, a team wins and the players leave the field.
explanation.walkthrough: A rubbish tip is a mess. 'men on board' looks like chess pieces but means sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Messmates are sailors who eat together on board a ship.

clue.text: End of pipe opens up containing energy leak

indicators.note: the reversed run holds the energy letter inside
in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top
End of means the final letter of pipe

parts.note: gapes means opens wide
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A pipe's end opens up and leaks energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns E and GAPES into SEPAGE; 'containing' then adds another E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid escaping slowly, a leak.

clue.text: Male type exceedingly soft?

parts.note: ilk means type or kind
so means very or exceedingly
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A description of a feeble man, very soft in nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a timid, unmanly weakling, a man of exceedingly soft character.

clue.text: Obscure band ends festival of Glastonbury initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words band ends festival of Glastonbury

explanation.surface: A band closes the Glastonbury festival, little known.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury Festival is a big music festival in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to make unclear or confuse, so to obscure.

clue.text: Country dance half finished by hard deluge

indicators.note: the half dance is followed and completed by the other pieces
half means only the first half of the dance word is used

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
rain is a downpour or deluge

explanation.surface: A country dance cut short by a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes BA from BALL. 'Country dance' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain is an island nation in the Persian Gulf, a country.

clue.text: Tablet provided elevated stimulation

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a pill is a tablet
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A pill that gives a lift, if you take it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'elevated' signals the pieces read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or stimulus that livens something up.

clue.text: They're useless without a sharp tip

definitions.text: They're useless without a sharp tip

indicators.note: without means the next letter is taken away from the useless word

parts.note: needless means unnecessary or useless

indicators.note: tip means the first letter of sharp

explanation.surface: A truism about things that need a point to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes S, the first letter of 'sharp', from NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing pins and syringes with blunt points cannot pierce anything, so they would be useless.

clue.text: Immorality supported by Church's following

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below

parts.note: sin is immorality
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Wickedness backed by the church gains followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' puts CE beneath SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Since means after, as in 'ever since then', so following in time.

clue.text: His heart's more robust adopting new medical device

indicators.note: the pieces take in the new letter among them
heart's means the middle letter of His

parts.note: haler means healthier, more robust

explanation.surface: A patient's heart grows stronger after taking a new device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts N after I, inside I+HALER.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device delivering medicine to the lungs, e.g. for asthma.

clue.text: Cleric beginning to preach inflammatory activity

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of preach

parts.note: arson is the crime of setting fires

explanation.surface: A cleric starts preaching fiery sermons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflammatory' suggests rousing speech but means literal fire-raising.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish priest, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Turn backwards perhaps, mistakenly — learning (to avoid repetitions!)

indicators.note: mistakenly says the remaining letters are set down wrongly, in a new order
learning has two Ns, so avoiding the repeat drops one of them

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside: the setter avoids repeating himself while learning from a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue, 'Something I learnt holding back side again', was faulty: reading 'somethiNG I LEARnt' backwards gives RAELIGN. The Telegraph replaced it online with this anagram clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to change orientation or allegiance, and turning backwards is one example of that.

clue.text: Glorious Queen in comeback finished gripping large finale

indicators.note: in comeback means the Queen letters are turned around

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: the finished word wraps around the following pieces

parts.note: spent means used up, finished
an end is a finale

explanation.surface: A queen returns, worn out but holding on for a big finish.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; 'in comeback' turns it round, and 'gripping' sets large and finale inside finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Resplendent means dazzling and splendid, so glorious.
